# Desktop apps

## Scope

Applies when the change touches macOS and Windows apps, Electron, Tauri, their signing, updater, and stores. Not when the change is a command-line tool or library with no installer, or a web app in a browser tab, which `aidd-team:web-front-end` covers. Neighbours: `aidd-team:secure-coding`, `aidd-team:release-rollout`, `aidd-team:web-front-end`.

## Checklist by loop step

| Step | Item | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Before the first edit (`aidd gate --paths`) | For a change to signing, entitlements, the updater, the installer, or a store listing, the author declares the security dimension (major). The release channel's rules are a dependency. | S1, S2, S3, S4 |
| Specify | Each channel named with its signing and update path (`references/distribution.md`). A Mac App Store build is sandboxed, updates only through the store, and has no license screen (2.4.5). | S4, S3, S1, S2 |
| Implement | Electron: context isolation and the sandbox on, and Node integration off in every renderer. A CSP; navigation, new windows, and IPC senders checked; no remote code; fuses flipped at package time. | S5 |
| Implement | Tauri: the fewest capabilities per window, a CSP, and the isolation pattern where the front end runs code it did not write. | S6 |
| Implement | Updates signed and verified before install (the Tauri updater's signature, Electron's updater on a signed build). The update key outside the repository. No downloaded code that changes described features (Store 10.2.2), and a Store game updates only through the Store (10.2.5). | S6, S5, S3 |
| Review | Each entitlement and hardened runtime exception has a reason in the Spec; none disables library validation without one. | S1 |
| Ship | macOS: Developer ID signed, hardened runtime, notarized, ticket stapled to the app, DMG, or PKG. Windows: every PE file signed and timestamped, chained to the Microsoft Trusted Root Program. | S1, S2, S3 |

## Test commands

| Command | Proves | How | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Gatekeeper assessment | macOS accepts the app as notarized Developer ID software | `spctl --assess --type execute --verbose=4 App.app` (`--type install` for a PKG) says accepted, source Notarized Developer ID | S1 |
| Stapled ticket check | the ticket travels with the download, for offline first launch | `xcrun stapler validate` on the app, DMG, or PKG | S1 |
| Authenticode verification | every Windows binary is signed, timestamped, and chains to a trusted root | `signtool verify /pa /all /v` on each PE file and the installer | S2, S3 |
| Electron fuse and preference check | the packaged app has its fuses set and every window its safe preferences | `npx @electron/fuses@2.1.3 read --app <packaged app>`; a test asserting each window's `webPreferences` | S5 |
| Signed update round trip | the updater installs a signed update and refuses a tampered one | a staging feed serving one package signed with the update key and one signed with another | S6, S5 |

## Owned elsewhere

- Rollout stages, beta channels, and the observe window: `aidd-team:release-rollout`.
- Pinned dependency, static, and secret scans: `aidd-team:enterprise-controls`.

## References

- [references/distribution.md](references/distribution.md): the channels (direct download, Mac App Store, Microsoft Store, Steam, package managers) with each one's signing, review, and update path.

## Keep it current

Each entry is due after its `review_every_days` (else emerging 90 days, established 365) or by its `review_due`. An emerging one applies only when the change needs it, said in the Spec. One `aidd eval standards` lists as due is looked up in Specify, and a missing one is proposed to aidd's `schemas/roles.json`.
